assessmentSummary.identity: A Rear Support Table Hold begins seated with both palms on the stable floor behind the hips, fingers forward or slightly outward, both feet fixed, knees bent to approximately 90 degrees, then lifts the hips to a table shape with straight or nearly straight arms, controlled shoulders, open chest, and no wrist collapse. Count only continuous valid hold seconds and lower hips under control to exit. It is not a straight-leg reverse plank, crab walk, bridge, hip thrust, shoulder extension mobility drill, push-up, knee lift, limb lift, raised or unstable support, assessment, or clinical intervention.
currentCardFindings: Source 76 provides a coherent bent-knee reverse-table support contract but lacks exact contacts, entry and exit, count unit, anatomy, dosage, fatigue, stop rules, relationships, media review, and calibration.

currentCardSnapshot.description: From a seated position on a clean stable floor or mat, put both palms behind the hips with fingers forward or slightly outward and both feet fixed with knees bent to approximately 90 degrees. Lift hips into a table shape with controlled shoulders, open chest, straight or nearly straight arms, and no wrist collapse. Count only continuous valid hold seconds; lower hips under control to exit. Finger direction, hand spacing, knee angle within the declared bent-knee table range, breath, hold seconds, rest, mat use, and cueing are delivery annotations. Straight-leg reverse planks, crab walks, bridges, hip thrusts, limb lifts, moving tasks, raised or unstable support, external load, assessments, and clinical interventions require their own reviewed definition or variant.
